item.title: Mortgage Rates Drop Slightly Amid Market Adjustments
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: Mortgage Rates Today, Thursday, November 5: A Little Lower
Mortgage rates fell slightly today to 7.01% APR, down six basis points from yesterday and 17 basis points from a week ago. The decline may be linked to post-midterm election clarity and lower oil prices. Tomorrow’s October jobs report could influence future rate movements, as steady employment data might strengthen the case for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its December meeting. The Fed’s federal funds rate indirectly affects mortgage rates, with lenders adjusting pricing based on expected rate changes. September’s inflation data showed a rise to 3.6% year-over-year, and October’s PCE report will be released on November 25. Experts advise refinancing if current rates are at least 0.5-0.75 percentage points lower than existing rates, though affordability and long-term goals should guide decisions. Rate locks are recommended if a favorable quote is secured, and personalized rates vary based on credit scores and financial profiles. Lenders adjust rates frequently, so locking in a rate provides protection against market fluctuations.

item.title: $10B deal that reduces Sempra’s LNG footprint about to get signed
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune
Sempra is finalizing a $10 billion deal to reduce its stake in liquefied natural gas (LNG) facilities. KKR and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board will purchase a 45% equity stake in Sempra Infrastructure Partners, a subsidiary. The transaction will cut Sempra’s ownership in key projects: Cameron LNG from 35.1% to 12.6%, Port Arthur LNG first phase from 19.6% to 7%, and Energía Costa Azul first phase from 58.4% to 20.9%. Sempra CEO Jeff Martin said the deal will simplify the company’s business model, with proceeds funding utility growth, debt reduction, and balance sheet strengthening. The shift focuses on U.S. regulated utilities, with 95% of earnings expected from utilities by next year. Sempra owns San Diego Gas & Electric, Southern California Gas, and 80% of Texas utility Oncor. Texas’s new Democratic governor, Gina Hinojosa, plans a data center moratorium, but Sempra executives emphasized bipartisan infrastructure support. Sempra reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $917 million, up 26% from 2025.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV Tours Latin America Post-Lung Cancer Surgery
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle, BBC News, NPR Topics: News Original headline: Pope Leo XIV Begins Latin America Tour Following Lung Cancer Surgery
Pope Leo XIV has begun a 12-day Latin America tour following lung cancer surgery, starting in Uruguay. The 71-year-old pope, born in the U.S., underwent right lung tumor removal three weeks ago. Vatican officials describe his health as stable, noting his 'fantastic stamina' and 'extreme enthusiasm' for the schedule. The trip, his longest and farthest as pope, includes stops in Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru. Uruguay, the most secular Latin American nation, has legalized marijuana, abortion, and same-sex marriage, yet the pope's visit drew sold-out tickets for a Montevideo prayer vigil. In Argentina, the pope will honor his predecessor Pope Francis, despite political tensions with President Javier Milei, who criticized the Church's social policies. The trip concludes in Peru, where Leo previously served, including a Mass in his former diocese and visits to the Amazon. The Vatican emphasizes the tour's role in reaffirming Catholic presence in a region with declining church influence. Street vendors and bakeries are selling pope-themed merchandise ahead of the visit.
item.source: Deutsche Welle, BBC News, NPR Topics: News

item.title: IRS Updates 2027 Tax Brackets for 2028 Filings
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: 2027 Tax Brackets and Federal Income Tax Rates
The IRS has released 2027 tax brackets, effective for 2028 tax filings. Tax rates remain unchanged from 2026, but brackets are adjusted for inflation to keep more income in lower tax brackets. For example, a single filer can earn up to $52,025 in 2027 and pay a top rate of 12%, compared to $50,400 in 2026. Tax brackets determine the highest rate applied to income within a specific bracket, with lower rates applying to income in lower brackets. The IRS explains that the top rate for a single filer earning $150,000 would apply to a portion of income at 24%, while the rest is taxed at 10%, 12%, and 22%. The agency provides tax bracket tables for single filers, married couples filing jointly, heads of household, and married couples filing separately. A tool created by the editorial team with AI assistance is available to calculate taxes owed for each filing status.

item.title: NASA Rocket Launch May Have Created Ionosphere Hole, Disrupted GPS
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Lunar rocket launch tore ‘hole’ in Earth’s atmosphere, disrupted GPS, study finds
A NASA rocket launch for the Artemis II lunar mission may have created disturbances in Earth’s ionosphere, according to a study by Taiwan’s National Cheng Kung University. Published in July’s Geophysical Research Letters, the research links the April 1 launch to three ionospheric perturbations, causing GPS positioning errors of several meters. The ionosphere, a region 30-600 miles above Earth, reflects radio waves critical for communication and navigation. Researchers warn such disruptions could affect autonomous vehicles and drones, with one expert noting "a couple of meters error is enough to cause an autonomous car to change lanes." While no real-world GPS failures or accidents were reported, the study highlights potential risks as rocket launches become more frequent. The findings suggest future missions could pose challenges for satellite-based systems, though no confirmed impacts were identified.

item.title: Fleet Week Offers Public Warship Tours and Free Concerts This Weekend
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Navy warship tours and free military band concerts open to public this weekend during Fleet Week
The public can tour three U.S. Navy warships and attend free military band concerts during Fleet Week in San Diego this weekend. Warship tours will take place Saturday from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Naval Base San Diego, requiring adults 18+ to show valid government-issued ID. Open ships include the littoral combat ship USS Jackson, Arleigh Burke-class destroyer USS Chafee, and Zumwalt-class destroyer USS Michael Monsoor. Concurrent events feature free performances: Marine Band San Diego plays at Jacobs Music Center Friday at 6 p.m., while Navy Band Southwest collaborates with civic organist Raul Preito Ramirez at Spreckels Organ Pavilion Sunday at 2 p.m. The Sunday concert includes an original organ and band composition commissioned by Fleet Week San Diego through a National Endowment of the Arts grant. Details available at fleetweeksandiego.org.

item.title: Coastal Commission Approves Sand and Seawall to Protect San Clemente Railway
item.description:
Source: LA Times, San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Coastal Commission Approves Sand and Seawall to Protect Vulnerable San Clemente Railway
The California Coastal Commission approved a shoreline protection plan to safeguard the San Clemente railway corridor from rising seas, storms, and erosion. The project includes 700,000 cubic yards of sand replenishment, the largest effort along this coast in over 60 years, and a 1,200-foot seawall. A 10-year permit balances immediate stabilization with long-term strategies, including potential rail line relocation. Orange County Supervisor Katrina Foley called sand replenishment critical for protecting the rail line’s buffer, noting previous hardening methods like seawalls can worsen erosion. The $300 million project aims to address 12 months of closures since 2021 due to erosion and bluff failures. Public concerns arose over rock revetments and seawalls, with San Clemente City Manager Andy Hall urging prioritization of beach replenishment. The plan requires monitoring sand movement and its impact on kelp and reef habitats, with a final report due in 10 years. Relocation remains a possibility but faces high costs and limited progress. Sand replenishment is set to begin in January, with ongoing studies on volume and frequency requirements.

item.title: Ukraine Evacuates Residents from Oleshky Amid Ceasefire Tensions
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Does the Oleshky ceasefire signal progress to come in Ukraine?
Nearly 800 residents were evacuated from Russia-occupied Oleshky, coordinated by Ukrainian Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets and Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova, with US First Lady Melania Trump credited for mediating. Over 1,000 people remain in the city, receiving aid. Trump praised the effort as a model for lasting peace, while Lubinets emphasized continued cooperation. The Kremlin denied further humanitarian plans. Ukraine accused Russia of using the ceasefire to reinforce military positions, citing drone footage of troop movements and equipment transport. Ukrainian officials acknowledged Russia’s likely exploitation of pauses but argued such missions remain necessary. The timing of the mission, just before US midterms, was seen as a political move for Trump’s image. Both sides gained publicity: Russia aimed to improve its image, while Washington sought to portray Trump as a peacemaker. Analysts questioned the ceasefire’s impact on upcoming Abu Dhabi talks, with skepticism about political progress despite potential humanitarian gains. Russia’s willingness to engage remains uncertain, with some experts believing Moscow is still buying time to avoid concessions.

item.title: Del Mar Sea Cave Collapse Sparks Erosion Concerns Amid El Niño Threats
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Sea cave damage raises concerns about Del Mar bluffs ahead of El Niño impact
A sea cave in Del Mar collapsed recently, prompting concerns about erosion and El Niño's impact. Chris Frydrych discovered the collapse while walking the beach, noting debris and a collapsed ceiling in an 8-foot-tall, 20-foot-deep cave. He warned that high tides and storms could worsen erosion, comparing the bluff's instability to an eggshell under pressure. Frydrych, who lives in a nearby condominium, expressed worry about a pending housing development near the site. The city called the incident a 'minor failure,' stating drone surveys found no cave collapse but noted sandstone layers fell near the opening. Officials emphasized coastal bluffs' natural fragility and urged beachgoers to stay clear. The area is also part of a court battle between the city and a developer over construction plans.

item.title: Snowflake's Former Revenue Chief Joins AI Startup Spectro Cloud
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Why Snowflake's former revenue chief is joining a little-known AI infrastructure startup
Mike Gannon, former revenue chief at Snowflake, is joining AI infrastructure startup Spectro Cloud as chief revenue officer. Gannon left Snowflake in April for personal reasons, with his departure described as mutually negotiated. Spectro Cloud, a $1 billion company, provides software for secure AI setup, cost management, and agent monitoring. The firm raised over $100 million in a July Series D round and aims for $100 million in annual recurring revenue. CEO Tenry Fu noted AI now accounts for more than half of Spectro's business, with annual growth of two- to threefold. Gannon cited parallels to his past roles at VMware and EMC, emphasizing opportunities in AI inference. Spectro's leadership upgrade also includes new chief marketing officer Peter Finter. The company is expanding into London, Washington, DC, and the Middle East, serving clients like T-Mobile, Airbus, and the US Air Force. Spectro claims to cut token costs for some customers by up to 90%.

item.title: Poway Unified outlines mold remediation plan at Del Sur Elementary
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Poway Unified provides update on Del Sur Elementary mold issue
Poway Unified School District outlined a comprehensive mold remediation plan for Del Sur Elementary School following months of delays. Officials confirmed the mold, identified as Cladosporium, is not highly toxic and not the common 'black mold.' The plan includes removing all flooring, fabric curtains, and other materials, along with installing a new HVAC system. The estimated cost of remaining work is $18.5 million, with completion targeted for July 9, 2027, and students returning in August 2027. District representatives emphasized ensuring the issue does not recur. Parents, including Steven Eisenberg, praised the thorough process and called for continued transparency to rebuild trust. All six board members approved the plan. Families remain concerned about the long-term impact on students, with Eisenberg noting the decision affects his children for over a decade. The district aims to restore a safe learning environment by the new school year.

item.title: European Airlines and Airports Hit by Hoax Bomb Threats Again
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Hoax bomb threats target European airlines and airports for second time in a week
At least 21 European flights and multiple airports faced bomb threats in a second incident this week, with UK officials labeling it a 'malicious hoax.' Flights to Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, France, Italy, Poland, and Romania were affected, including diverted Aer Lingus and Finnair flights escorted by fighter jets. No explosives were found during inspections. Threats were attributed to a group calling itself 'Fighters of the Male State,' linked to Russia's banned ultra-right 'Muzhskoi Legion.' Airport authorities in Rome confirmed the threats via email, though no credible leads have emerged. UK Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander called the incidents hoaxes but emphasized the government's serious approach. Airlines like EasyJet and Ryanair reported affected flights, with passengers experiencing delays and security checks. Experts warned that frequent hoaxes could erode trust in threat assessments, though some viewed the incidents as part of a pattern of disruptive actions. Two days prior, similar threats had led to flight searches without finding explosives.

item.title: High Rates Prompt Reconsideration of Adjustable-Rate Mortgages
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Economy Original headline: With stubbornly high interest rates, some are reconsidering adjustable-rate mortgages
High interest rates are prompting some borrowers to reconsider adjustable-rate mortgages. With 30-year fixed-rate mortgages at 7% or higher, ARMs—once stigmatized after the 2008 crisis—are gaining attention. Analysis shows ARMs have historically offered advantages, with 70% of borrowers able to refinance into lower rates over time. Chen Zhao of Rocket Mortgage notes that while rates could reset upward, they've often reset downward, making ARMs cost-effective. However, experts caution that past low rates may not repeat, and emotional factors influence loan decisions. Fixed-rate mortgages remain popular for their predictability, despite higher costs. Regulators have tightened ARM safeguards since the financial crisis, requiring borrowers to qualify for rates above initial teaser rates. While ARMs could offer savings, their appeal remains limited due to uncertainty and borrower anxiety.

item.title: Carpenter Turns Storage Yard Business into Financial Freedom
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: How a carpenter went from bankrupt to financially independent with a novel business of renting dirt
Chris Long, a former carpenter and construction company owner in Ottawa, Canada, founded Longyards to solve his own storage needs. The company rents secure outdoor storage yards to contractors on a month-to-month basis, offering flexible, gated spaces for equipment and materials. After a failed construction job left him with limited funds, Long purchased a 10-acre property but faced a tight two-year deadline to repay a seller-financed loan. The first yard opened on October 1, 2019, without tenants, but he secured leases within six weeks, attracting a roofer, electrician, landscaper, and RV operator. This traction helped him repay the loan. Long expanded to Florida and Texas, prioritizing demand over cheap land. He emphasizes the business's complexity, including zoning, permits, and security, noting there's no established playbook. Long claims one storage yard now generates more income than his previous construction business, allowing him financial freedom. 'Simple cash flow creates freedom,' he said, transitioning from bankruptcy to financial independence through this novel storage model.

item.title: Block offers 90 days pay and healthcare for US laid-off workers
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Here's the severance package Block is offering laid-off US employees
Block is offering laid-off US employees a severance package including at least 60 days of pay, seven weeks of base pay plus an additional week for each year worked, and 30 days of pay if they sign a separation agreement. Healthcare benefits include three months of COBRA premium coverage for employees and dependents, along with a one-time $5,000 transition payment. The package differs from February's offer, which included 20 weeks of salary and six months of healthcare coverage. Block’s latest cuts, part of a second round of layoffs this year, did not cite AI as a reason, instead referencing improved tools for handling routine tasks. Affected workers will also receive a prorated payment in place of a 2027 retention bonus. The company’s benefits are contingent on signing the separation agreement. Block’s layoffs follow better-than-expected third-quarter profits. Other firms like Canva and Squarespace also announced staff reductions with similar severance terms.

item.title: Airbnb CEO says AI agents like Muse and Instinct are barely bringing in bookings: 'I don't see them as a threat'
item.description:
Source: Business Insider
Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky said AI agents like Meta's Muse and Instinct are not significantly impacting bookings, noting low traffic and fewer conversions. During the third quarter earnings call, Chesky described agent-driven bookings as 'very non-material' compared to Airbnb's daily half-million reservations. He added that traffic from agents peaked in early October and has not increased since. Chesky views AI agents as an opportunity to expand Airbnb's reach, comparing them to Google, and plans to launch a specialized travel AI agent in early 2024. He argued general AI agents are not ideal for complex tasks like trip planning, which he calls 'aspirational' and requires human input. Chesky highlighted that 80% of travelers enjoy the planning process, often messaging hosts and reviewing multiple listings. He also noted most traffic occurs during work hours, suggesting users are using Airbnb discreetly. Other travel companies like Booking.com and Expedia also reported minimal traffic from AI agents, with DoorDash CEO Tony Xu citing 'several hundred orders' from third-party agents.

item.title: Bird Rock Tree Replacement Scheduled for Next Month
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Toppled tree in Bird Rock expected to be replaced next month
A Canary Island pine tree in Bird Rock's median toppled after repeated vandalism. Incisions to its base were first noted Feb. 13, with additional cuts reported by Barbara Dunbar, a BRCC board member, on May 6. The tree fell around 4:30 a.m. on May 9 despite crews placing caution tape. No injuries or vehicle damage occurred. A felony vandalism report was filed with San Diego police. Replacement is scheduled for next month, with a semi-mature 24-inch box tree set for December planting. The estimated cost, including cleanup and new tree, is $30,000, funded by the Maintenance Assessment District. Dunbar highlighted Urban Landcare's transition to electronic tools during her annual MAD report, noting reduced vandalism and improved maintenance. Halloween saw minimal damage due to security and weather. The BRCC will host a holiday party in December instead of a regular meeting.

item.title: Santa Ana Winds Bring Heat and Fire Risk in November
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: Near 90 in November as Santa Anas bring fire risk plus heat, especially along the coast
Santa Ana winds are arriving in Southern California, bringing heat and fire danger. Meteorologist Rich Thompson of the National Weather Service reported weak to moderate winds developing Thursday, peaking Saturday with gusts up to 55 mph in mountain areas. Temperatures are forecast to reach near 90, with coastal regions experiencing highs of 84-87 degrees. Red flag warnings are in effect for Los Angeles and Ventura counties, highlighting critical fire threats due to warm, dry conditions. The weather service noted coastal areas like San Diego and Orange counties could see temperatures 10-20 degrees above normal. Previous Santa Ana winds fueled fires, including the 570-acre Norte fire in San Clemente. Officials are monitoring whether lessons from past fires, such as the Eaton and Palisades blazes, have been applied. An atmospheric river event may bring rain weekend of Nov. 13-14, though details remain uncertain.

item.title: Thinking Machines Lab closes $5B funding round at $40B valuation
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Thinking Machines Lab is closing in on a new $5 billion funding round at a $40 billion valuation
Thinking Machines Lab is closing a $5 billion funding round at a $40 billion pre-money valuation, led by Accel. The startup, founded by Mira Murati, previously raised $2 billion last year and was valued over $10 billion. This round triples its last public valuation, reflecting continued investor confidence despite intensified AI talent competition. The company, which emerged from stealth last year, released an updated version of its Tinker tool, showing gains in AI coding. However, it has lost key founders like Barret Zoph and Andrew Tulloch to rivals like Meta and OpenAI. About a third of its founding team has left, driven by competitive pay offers. The Information reported earlier talks for a new funding round in September. A TML representative declined comment, and Accel did not respond to inquiries.

item.title: Nvidia Faces Risks as Neoclouds Struggle with Financial Pressures
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: As neoclouds face a financial reckoning, Nvidia has to decide how far to go to help
Neoclouds, which rent AI computing power, face financial strain as construction delays, regulatory concerns, and tighter lending conditions threaten their viability. Nvidia, a key supporter, is deepening its involvement by guaranteeing construction financing for a West Virginia data center for Nscale, a neocloud firm building for Anthropic. If Nscale defaults, Nvidia could assume ownership of the multibillion-dollar facility. Nvidia’s $36 billion support program, which includes commitments to cover unused compute costs, has drawn antitrust scrutiny, prompting pauses in some deals. Alex Yeh, CEO of Nvidia-backed GMI, emphasized the need for selectivity, stating, 'You have limited capital, even as big as Nvidia.' Gartner predicts 80% of neoclouds will cease independent operations by 2030, leading to consolidation. Larger firms may acquire assets like data centers or customer contracts rather than entire companies, as Yeh noted, 'I would acquire strategic assets.'

item.title: Coastal flooding advisory issued for San Diego County beaches
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Coastal flooding advisory issued for San Diego County beaches as big tides and strong waves draw near
A coastal flood advisory is in effect for San Diego County beaches from noon Friday to noon Tuesday due to El Niño-driven high tides and approaching strong waves. Forecasters predict tides will reach 7.4 feet Saturday and 7.5 feet or higher Sunday, with waves between 3-5 feet and occasional 6-7 foot sets. These conditions could cause minor run-ups, flooding at Mission Beach boardwalk and coastal parking lots, and wave impacts on seawalls. Erosion risks are heightened as seasonal shifts direct larger waves toward beaches. A surge sent water to the base of cliffs at Blacks Beach on Thursday. Weekend temperatures will hit 86°F Saturday and 88°F Sunday, higher than the seasonal average of 73°F. Warm ocean temperatures, 74-76°F, have led to sightings of rare fish species like razor surgeonfish and three-banded butterflyfish in local waters, including La Jolla Cove.

item.title: San Marcos Student Airlifted After Injury During Lunch
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Student airlifted from San Marcos Middle School after injury on lower track field during lunch
A San Marcos Middle School student was airlifted to a hospital after sustaining an injury during lunch on the school's lower track field. Emergency personnel responded to the incident, with a medical helicopter landing in a parking lot adjacent to the school. The student was rushed into the helicopter by five emergency workers before being transported for medical care. The school briefly implemented a Hold and Secure protocol to ensure the helicopter could land safely, then resumed normal operations after emergency personnel cleared the area. The district confirmed the student was injured while playing on the track field and noted the school's response to the situation. No further details about the injury or the student's condition were provided.

item.title: Sweden constructs homes using modular factory methods
item.description:
Source: Vox Original headline: Sweden builds houses and apartments like Lego sets. Why don’t we?
Sweden constructs homes using modular factory methods, assembling entire rooms with pre-fabricated components. Companies like Ikea pioneered this approach, with 90% of new single-family homes and 43% of multifamily apartments built using prefabricated timber systems. Modular units, including kitchens and bathrooms with plumbing and wiring, are transported and assembled on-site in weeks. Experts note the U.S. lags in adopting these methods, despite Sweden’s success in efficient, high-quality housing. Challenges include outdated building codes and zoning regulations, which hinder innovation. While the U.S. experimented with prefabrication in the 1960s through programs like Operation Breakthrough, these efforts failed to scale. Analysts argue that improving regulatory frameworks, rather than focusing solely on modular construction, is key to advancing factory-built housing in the U.S. Sweden’s approach, blending industrialized construction with standardized processes, offers a model for addressing housing shortages globally.

item.title: Bus Crash in Eastern France Kills 2, Injures 16
item.description:
Source: BBC News, Deutsche Welle Original headline: Bus Crash in Eastern France Claims Two Lives, Injuries Reported
A bus carrying schoolchildren crashed in eastern France near Lent on Friday morning, killing at least two people and injuring 16 others, including three in critical condition. The vehicle, traveling between Lyon and Bourg-en-Bresse, left the road and struck a tree in a ditch around 07:00 local time. Mayor Yves Cristin described the scene as an 'absolute tragedy,' noting the road was slightly damp but no major weather hazards were reported. The bus's side was torn off, likely causing severe injuries to those on that side. Over 100 firefighters and 50 police officers were deployed, with the road closed for investigation. The bus carried 43 passengers, including 15 minors. An investigation into homicide by vehicle has begun, though the driver, hospitalized with injuries, has not yet been questioned. Medical helicopters transported critically injured victims to a specialized hospital. French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot and Education Minister Édouard Geffray expressed condolences, with Geffray calling the incident 'always difficult when our children are victims of accidents of this nature.' Deutsche Welle noted the crash site had no major road difficulties, but the presence of a tree in the bus's path worsened the accident's severity. The exact cause remains under investigation.

item.title: Global markets plunge as AI spending fears trigger sell-off across Europe, Asia, and US
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
European shares fell sharply as a global sell-off driven by AI spending fears spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe. The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out weekly gains, with media, healthcare, and retail stocks leading declines. Japanese and South Korean markets also tumbled, with Tokyo's Nikkei 225 falling 5.5% and Seoul's Kospi slumping 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker. Asian tech giants like Samsung, SK Hynix, and TSMC saw steep declines, with Samsung down nearly 10% and SK Hyn, over 11%. US markets were hit hard on Thursday, with the Nasdaq plunging 5.52% and the S&P 500 dropping 4.4%. Concerns over AI spending plans and potential regulatory curbs, amplified by Democratic control of Congress, fueled investor anxiety. Democratic governors-elect campaigned on slowing AI development and halting data center construction. Michael McCarthy of Moomoo noted the shift in market sentiment, citing sharp swings as a sign of a turning point.

item.title: First-Time Homebuyers Pay All Cash at Record High Despite Low Numbers
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Business Original headline: First-time homebuyers remain scarce, but a record share of them pay all cash
First-time homebuyers remain at a near-record low of 22% according to the National Association of Realtors, but a record 10% pay all cash. Jessica Lautz, deputy chief economist at NAR, attributes this trend to inheritances, noting first-time buyers who paid all-cash were more likely to use inheritance funds (28%) or proceeds from inherited property sales (21%). The median age of all first-time buyers is 40, a record high, with all-cash buyers averaging 54. Personal savings remains the primary down payment source, but more buyers are using assets like 401(k)s, stocks, or crypto than family financial help. Real estate agents report a surge in all-cash offers since the pandemic, driven by high mortgage rates and generational wealth transfers. Some buyers refinance into mortgages after closing. Younger buyers like Seth Esmeson, who face debt and high prices, struggle to enter the market, citing the growing gap between generations. They express frustration over the market’s favoring older buyers and reluctance to rely on inheritances.

item.title: Study Suggests Cannabis Use 2,800 Years Ago in Siberian Tomb
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Seeds, preserved hair in tomb point to oldest signs of cannabis high 2,800 years ago, study suggests
Archaeologists in Siberia found cannabis seeds and preserved human hair in a 2,800-year-old tomb, suggesting ancient cannabis use predates previous records by 300 years. The study, led by teams from Germany, Russia, Sweden, and Switzerland, analyzed hair from the Scythian-era tomb at Tunnug 1, where cannabis seeds were also discovered. Co-author Gino Caspari noted the rarity of finding both plant material and human tissue with active compounds. Radiocarbon dating confirmed the seeds’ age, and their placement in the tomb implies cultural significance. However, experts like Volker Auwaerter criticized the hair analysis as scientifically weak, arguing the data lacks evidence to confirm cannabis consumption over external exposure. The study, published in Science, faces skepticism due to the inability to distinguish use from environmental contact. Scholars emphasize the need for forensic toxicology tests to validate the findings, as cannabis has non-psychoactive uses like oil and fiber production.
